chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding ten people who jointly killed a man, he said: 'The family of the slain may choose any one of them to kill, and his heirs will claim nine-tenths of the blood money from the remaining nine.'
ai.seo_question: How is blood money divided when ten people jointly kill one person?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *kaffa'ah* (joint liability) in Shia jurisprudence, where the victim's heirs hold the option to select a single perpetrator for *qisas* (retribution) while retaining the right to claim the full *diyah* from the group. The specific allocation of nine-tenths to the remaining nine co-perpetrators highlights the proportional distribution of financial compensation among those not chosen for execution, reflecting the nuanced application of equity in blood money cases.
